(File photo) By: Uday Gupta Nov 17, 2026 20:20 IST Last Updated Nov 17, 2026 20:20 IST Published by Vivek Nov 17, 2026 20:20 IST Edited by Vivek Kumar In an unexpected turn of events that transpired during a family farewell at Kanpur railways station, 12 people who boarded a Vande Bharat Express to see off their relatives were unable to get off before its automatic doors closed. The Varanasi-New Delhi train was eventually halted at Etawah Junction, where railway authorities fined the group Rs 36,140 for travelling without valid tickets or platform tickets.
 advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story The incident took place on Sunday, November 15, when train number 22415 arrived at Kanpur Central at 9:26 am and departed at 9:30 am.
 The 12 adults, belonging to different parts of Kanpur, had entered the coaches to help their relatives settle in and manage their luggage. However, before they could get off, the train's automatic doors locked and it began moving.
 Realising they were trapped inside, the group approached onboard railway staff for assistance. However, they were reportedly informed that the train could not be stopped immediately.
 As some members began creating a commotion, railway personnel alerted the Tundla control room, following which an unscheduled halt was arranged at Etawah Junction.
 The train reached Etawah at around 10:50 am, after the group had spent nearly 79 minutes onboard.
 The 12 individuals were subsequently escorted to the Railway Protection Force (RPF) post, where railway commercial staff issued a penalty of Rs 3,000 to each person for travelling without valid tickets or platform tickets. The total amount collected was Rs 36,140, according to reports.
 RPF Inspector Dinesh Kumar Singh said the action was taken because the individuals did not possess platform tickets and had also created a disturbance onboard.
 After paying the penalty, they were allowed to leave and warned against repeating the mistake. HOW OTHER PASSENGERS SEE IT
 Meanwhile, the incident has triggered discussions over passenger safety, platform access and the automatic door-locking mechanism on premium trains.
 An India Today team spoke to passengers at Pandit Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Junction in Uttar Pradesh to understand their views on the issue.
 Several passengers suggested introducing clearer warnings and alarm systems to prevent people from getting trapped.
 One of the passengers waiting for their train suggested installing a timer near train doors or reconsidering the existing system to avoid inconvenience. Others, however, felt that people accompanying passengers should be more careful about the train's departure timings.
 Rajan Upadhyay said only those genuinely required to assist with luggage should accompany passengers onto trains. He pointed out that several people often turn up to see off a single traveller, creating unnecessary congestion.
 Another passenger suggested restricting platform access to ticket-holding travellers, similar to the system followed in Metro stations.
 He also stressed that platform tickets should be made mandatory to prevent overcrowding, particularly during festivals.
 advertisement While automatic doors are intended to improve operational efficiency and regulate train access, the incident has highlighted the need for greater awareness among passengers and better crowd management.
 The Railways may face renewed calls for clearer departure alerts and stricter platform-entry regulations to ensure that such incidents are avoided. - Ends
